proposed.explanation:
EFID shows strong and accelerating profitability: revenue grew ~29.5% (from 16.15 B EGP to 20.92 B EGP), gross profit grew ~44.2%, and net profit grew ~67.7% (from 1.61 B to 2.70 B EGP). EPS doubled from 1.09 to 2.18 EGP. At the current price of 20.40 EGP, the trailing P/E is roughly 9.4×, which is low relative to the pace of earnings growth, suggesting the market may not yet fully price in the company's trajectory. Gross margin expanded from ~30.9% to ~34.4% and net margin from ~10.0% to ~12.9%, indicating improving operating leverage.

For your profile—5-7 year horizon, no liquidity needs, high loss tolerance—this growth profile is well suited. However, your medium financial capacity to absorb losses means I am capping the position at the diversification limit (≤50% of total portfolio value). Buying 1,225 shares costs 24,990 EGP, leaving 5,010 EGP in cash; EFID would represent 49.98% of the 50,000 EGP portfolio, satisfying the 50% cap.

Risks and limitations: I only have two years of income-statement data. There is no balance-sheet information (leverage, cash reserves), no dividend history, no segment or competitive-position detail, and no forward guidance. A single year of strong growth does not guarantee continuation. The stock could decline if growth decelerates or macro conditions worsen. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns. I recommend monitoring subsequent quarterly results and keeping the remaining cash available to diversify into other names as you build the portfolio over time.
